item.title: LPG shortage forces Bhubaneswar hotels, restaurants to return to wood stove
item.description: Bhubaneswar: The impact of the ongoing conflict in the Middle East has started affecting business and tourism in Odisha, with hotels and restaurants in Bhubaneswar facing severe difficulties due to a shortage of commercial LPG cylinders. With the supply of commercial LPG reportedly disrupted, many hotels and restaurants in the state capital have been forced to return to traditional wood stoves to continue their operations. item.title: Odisha Congress shifts its MLA to Bengaluru resort amid Rajya Sabha cross-voting worries
item.description: Bengaluru: Amid fears of cross-voting in the upcoming Rajya Sabha election in Odisha, the Congress party has shifted its MLAs to Bengaluru in a move widely seen as part of “resort politics” to keep its legislators together. Congress sources confirmed on Friday that the legislators were brought to Bengaluru under the supervision of Karnataka Deputy Chief Minister and State Congress President D.K. Shivakumar. item.title: Odisha: Major fire breaks out at Mancheswar Railway Wagon repair workshop
item.description: Bhubaneswar: A major fire broke out at the Mancheswar Railway Wagon repair workshop in Bhubaneswar in Odisha on Thursday night, causing damage to materials and equipment. The fire intensified quickly, spreading from the coach to the surrounding area within minutes. Stocks of both new and used repair equipment, as well as items like timber, plastic coverings, foam, plywood, and mattress padding, were engulfed in flames. item.title: Odisha: Two truck drivers killed in deadly crash on Bargarh-Sambalpur NH
item.description: Bargarh/Sambalpur: Two truck drivers were killed following a major road accident on the Bargarh–Sambalpur National Highway in Odisha late on Thursday night. The tragic mishap took place near Dharmashala Chhak under Atabira police limits, where two trucks collided head-on. item.description: Rayagada: In a brazen act of robbery, a group of armed miscreants attacked and looted a government employee at gunpoint in Rayagada town of Odisha late on Thursday night. item.description: Bhubaneswar: Concern over rising digital addiction among children in Odisha was raised in the State Assembly today as the 2025-26 Economic Survey has revealed that nearly two-thirds of children in the state are affected by excessive digital usage. item.title: Supreme Court declines plea for mandatory menstrual leave, says policy decision for Government
item.description: New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Friday declined to entertain a plea seeking mandatory menstrual leave for working women and female students across the country, observing that such a matter falls within the domain of government policy. item.title: Birla Global University Hosts International Conference on Grassroots & Frugal Innovation in Emerging Economies (GFI 2026)
item.description: Bhubaneswar: Birla Global University (BGU) hosts the International Conference on “Grassroots & Frugal Innovation in Emerging Economies (GFI 2026)” from 12–14 March 2026 at its Bhubaneswar campus.
